title: Speier et al. 2017 — A comparison of stimulus types in online classification of the P300 speller using language models
description: EEG recordings from 10 healthy participants performing an online P300 row-column speller task with a 6x6 character matrix. The study compares two stimulus types (Famous Faces and Inverting) combined with language-model-based classification. Data were recorded across two sessions per subject with 32 channels at 256 Hz and are distributed in BIDS format via MOABB.
methods_description: 32-channel EEG was recorded with a g.tec amplifier at 256 Hz, referenced to the left ear with ground at AFz. Participants used a P300 row-column speller with a 6x6 matrix, a stimulus onset asynchrony of 125 ms and an inter-stimulus interval of 25 ms. Each subject completed 2 sessions of 3 runs each, with visual feedback given online.
